q: 1. The term used to spread the cost of an asset over the span of several years is
explain: Depreciation is the accounting/engineering term used to allocate (spread) the cost of an asset over its useful life span.

q: 2. Net present value is the difference between
options: The present value of cash inflow and present value of outflows
explain: Net Present Value (NPV) is calculated as the present value of all cash inflows minus the present value of all cash outflows of a project.
Value is the present worth of a property, which can differ from the historical cost.

q: 4. The value of structure without being dismantled at the end of its utility period is known as:
explain: The value of a property at the end of its useful life, without being dismantled, is the salvage (or savage) value.

q: 5. If the net income is calculated with the rental method of valuation then, the net income is then,
options: a difference of gross income with all outgoing expenses
a product of actual cost and depreciation
a addition of original cost and annual depreciation
a difference of original cost and scrap-
explain: Net Income = Gross Rent - Outgoings (taxes, repairs, management, etc.).

q: 6. Total expenditure on annual repair and special repairs to a building should not be more than ........ of the capital cost
explain: As per standard maintenance norms, total annual/special repair expenditure is limited to about 2.5% of the building's capital cost.

the sum of money to be paid to authorities by the tenants
the fund for rebuilding structure its economic life is over
raised to meet the maintenance costs of the structure before dismantling
explain: A sinking fund is a fund created by setting aside annual installments so that at the end of the utility period, the accumulated amount is enough to replace the structure.
Valuation is required for various purposes including sale, tax assessment, and securing bank loans.

q: 9. In a linear depreciation method of property valuation depreciation is imposed on costs related to:
explain: Land does not depreciate; depreciation is applied to the building structure which has a finite life.

q: 10. Annual rent is generally fixed at:
explain: Annual rent is typically estimated between 5% and 10% of the capitalized value of the building.

q: 11. Which of the following has the least life?
explain: Among these, paint has by far the shortest useful life (needing frequent renewal, typically a few years), compared to the much longer lives of roads and brick work.

Salvage value (value of the structure intact at the end of its life) is generally greater than scrap value (value of dismantled/broken-down material), since dismantling reduces the material's usability and value.

q: 13. The total cost construction including cost of land is termed as
explain: Capital cost is defined as the total cost of a project, including both the cost of construction and the cost of the land on which it stands.
